meta.title: LLMInjection · AI Threat Landscape
meta.description: Open threat intelligence for LLM, AI and agentic systems: actors, campaigns, techniques, detections and evidence.
hero.title: Threat landscape for LLM and agentic systems
hero.dek: Who is using AI against whom, how the attacks work, and what detects or stops them. Every claim carries a source grade and a confidence level.
search.placeholder: Search actor, campaign, technique, CVE, control
data.notice: Record content (names, summaries, source titles) is in English. Search matches the English text.
dash.title: The state of the evidence
dash.sub: Computed from the graph and datasets on every build. Click anything with an underline to open its record.
dash.gaps.note: Techniques with linked evidence but no test or detection.
gaps.none: No technique with linked evidence lacks a test or detection.
gaps.next: Next in the queue: techniques without a control.
dash.conf.note: Records with a confidence rating: {n}. Sources and frameworks are graded separately.
dash.maturity.note: As evidenced in this repository. A low level means few links so far, not that a technique is theoretical.
dash.eco.note: Projects: {n}; flagged start here: {s}. None can support attribution.
actors.title: Who is operating
actors.sub: Vendor tracking labels are kept as published; aliases are not merged without evidence.
dom.title: Where it is moving
dom.sub: Direction of travel per domain, with the defensive focus that follows.

land.sub: Each figure keeps its original population and time window. Do not compare across rows.
land.sectors.sub: Single-source figures from the cited reports.
land.leads.sub: Claims held back until a primary source is attached.
new.title: What's new
new.sub: Entity-level changes against the latest committed monthly snapshot.
new.nochanges: No changes since the latest snapshot.
graph.title: Intelligence graph
graph.sub: One column per object type. Hover or focus a node to trace it; click or press Enter to open its record.
graph.kbd: Keyboard: arrow keys move between nodes, Enter opens a record.
cov.title: Technique coverage
cov.sub: Counted from the graph, the ecosystem and the files in detections/. Counts show design coverage: a detection counts even when it is only a specification, which is why the rule marker matters.
tl.title: Campaigns, incidents and vulnerabilities
tl.sub: Newest first, by the date of the primary report where known.
eco.title: Ecosystem map
eco.sub: Discovery and test-design material, classified by what each project can support. None can support attribution or campaign claims. State cross-checked by shallow clone; the archive flag comes from the GitHub API.
src.title: Source registry
src.sub: A = primary or authoritative, B = strong secondary, C = reputable press, D = community, E = unsupported.
lang.title: Translations
lang.sub: Choose the interface language. Translations are machine-assisted and have not yet been reviewed by native speakers; corrections are welcome.
lang.table.title: Available material
lang.scope.title: What is and is not translated
lang.scope.yes: Translated: the Explorer interface, the README and, in Spanish and Portuguese, the Latin America regional overview.
lang.scope.no: Not translated: record content such as actor, campaign and technique names, summaries and source titles. They quote primary reports, and a machine translation of an attribution statement could change its meaning.
lang.scope.search: Search and CSV exports use the English data. CSV files include a byte-order mark so Excel shows accents and non-Latin text correctly.
footer.tagline: Evidence over hype. Generated from validated repository data.
cov.view.label: View
cov.show.label: Show
cov.stale: Newest evidence is more than {n} days older than the latest in the dataset
cov.empty: No technique matches the current filters.
cov.unavailable: Coverage data (coverage.json) did not load. Reload, or run scripts/coverage_model.py locally.
cov.actors.note: A filled square means the actor conducts a campaign that uses the technique. Select it to open that campaign.
cov.note: Counts show design coverage, not tested coverage: {rules} of {total} detections exist as rule files, the rest are specifications. Newest dated evidence: {asof}.
cov.formula.title: How priority is scored
cov.formula: Priority = maturity weight (observed 4, disclosed vulnerability 3, research 2, none 1) x (4 - layers). Layers: a safe test, a detection (1 if a rule file exists, 0.5 if only a specification), a control and a benchmark, one point each. Higher means more urgent.
cov.rules: detections that exist as rule files
